name: Captopril
route_note: oral tablet two or three times daily, one hour before meals
originator: Squibb (Miguel Ondetti, David Cushman, Bernard Rubin)

discovery.by: Miguel Ondetti and David Cushman, Squibb
discovery.note: Designed from peptides in Bothrops jararaca snake venom studied by Sérgio Ferreira, using a model of the ACE active site.

tagline: First ACE inhibitor, rationally designed from Brazilian pit viper venom
summary: Captopril was the first orally active angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor and an early example of structure-based drug design, inspired by bradykinin-potentiating peptides from pit viper venom. It treats hypertension, heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction and diabetic nephropathy.
mechanism: Angiotensin-converting enzyme converts angiotensin I to the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II and also breaks down bradykinin. Inhibiting it lowers angiotensin II, causing vasodilation, reduced aldosterone secretion and less sodium retention, while bradykinin accumulates.
Captopril binds the zinc ion in ACE through a sulfhydryl (thiol) group. This group is linked to side effects such as taste disturbance and rash that are less common with later ACE inhibitors.

In the kidney, reduced efferent arteriolar constriction lowers glomerular pressure and proteinuria. Bradykinin accumulation contributes to vasodilation and is thought to cause the characteristic dry cough and, rarely, angioedema.
uses: Left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction

history.title: Venom peptides
history.detail: Sérgio Ferreira reports bradykinin-potentiating factors in Bothrops jararaca venom.

history.title: Captopril designed
history.detail: Ondetti and Cushman at Squibb design captopril from a hypothetical model of ACE.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Capoten.

history.title: SAVE
history.detail: Captopril reduces mortality in left ventricular dysfunction after MI.

history.title: Diabetic nephropathy
history.detail: Captopril slows kidney function decline in type 1 diabetic nephropathy.

history.title: Lasker Award
history.detail: Ondetti and Cushman receive the Lasker Clinical Medical Research Award.

safety.boxed_warning: Fetal toxicity: drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus; discontinue when pregnancy is detected.

facts: Captopril is often cited as one of the first successful examples of structure-based drug design.

references.title: Pfeffer MA et al. Effect of captopril on mortality and morbidity in patients with left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction (SAVE). N Engl J Med 1992
